facts.fact: MCC states that a pregnant woman who tests negative for HIV or TB at a rural health centre has her care recorded on paper, in a health booklet she carries, while an HIV-positive patient's care is recorded in an electronic medical record; MCC gives no date, so the document's is used.
facts.system: paper record and patient-held health booklet

facts.fact: MCC states that it plans to work with the Ministry of Health to design and implement a fully operational digital health system across all disease areas, building on what PEPFAR established, with major investment in digital health infrastructure beginning in early 2024; it names no domestic funding.

systems.system: electronic medical record for HIV-positive patients
systems.owner: built on PEPFAR and Global Fund investment
systems.tiers: rural health centres, for HIV-positive patients; linked to the national health information system, pharmacy and laboratory systems
non-HIV patient information is manually tabulated and entered; where is not stated

systems.owner: Ministry of Health with MCC, through the Millennium Challenge Account
systems.tiers: planned for primary health care, all disease areas

note: The existing electronic medical record is classed tracker: this document says it serves HIV-positive (and by implication TB) patients only, so its presence at rural health centres gives no emr fact. No hmis digitised fact: non-HIV data is manually tabulated and entered into the national system, but the document does not say at which level. The planned system is classed emr on 'across all disease areas'. The document's date is a proxy by its frontmatter.
